events.question: How can AI make us all money?
events.blurb: Opening night. AI may grow the pie while taking the jobs people have used to earn a slice. If machines do more of the making, how do the rest of us still get paid? Tonight we sit with that question as a room, not as an audience.
setup: One path we may walk is a citizens dividend from robot and compute permits: a check that follows the machines, not the old job. It could be a promising way to share what AI creates. It could be a trap. We will treat it as a live thread — something to help work through — not a finished answer.

Nightly 365 is collaborative. The host holds the question. Chat, callers, and the community think it through together. You are invited to help, to doubt out loud, or to follow along. Not a lecture. A gathering.

expect.before: Show up a few minutes early. Open the chat. Bring a thought, a doubt, or a small idea — whatever you are carrying is enough. If you would rather listen, that helps too. The night is free to watch.
expect.during: We open, then sit with the question long enough to feel why it is worth a night. We think together. If we need a way in, three doors are ready: how people still get a slice, whether a citizens dividend from permits holds, and what happens to work, status, and politics when the check shows up. If the room is already moving, we skip the doors. We close with one thing we found, any progress from the night, and a look at tomorrow.

subquestions: If AI grows the pie while taking jobs, how do people still get a slice?
A citizens dividend from robot and compute permits — promising path or trap?
When the check shows up, what happens to work, status, and politics?
events.join: Come to the live chat on YouTube. Help us work the question — or follow along and see what comes out of tonight. If you have something you want to say, the room will make space. First time is welcome.
ideas: If a data center drinks your town’s power and water, why don’t your neighbors get a check?
Alaska got oil checks. What’s our compute check?
Don’t ask AI for a job — ask who owns the machines.
Permits are the new payroll.
Your ZIP hosts the GPUs → your ZIP gets a cut.
Meter the power before they flip the switch; don’t beg for scraps after the IPO.
A claim signup beats a petition that dies in a drawer.
The first million people who claim a share of the machine layer win the story.
A host dividend isn’t anti-business — it’s the price of certainty.
Economic development that raises residential rates is just cost-shifting with a ribbon.
Don’t ask “will it create jobs?” Ask “will my neighbor get a check before they get a job offer?”
Megawatts raise the fire load — the host fee should rise with it.
Put the chief in the room before entitlement, not after the first alarm.
Certainty for the campus includes knowing the ZIP won’t revolt — that certainty has a price, and it’s the host check.
If the campus raises rents, the host check is partial rent control delivered by mail.
Don’t celebrate construction jobs while the apartment next door jumps $400 — put both numbers on one slide.
An equal host check is the only housing benefit that doesn’t need a waitlist.
Insurance premiums are the quiet host tax.
The mutuals spread a data center’s fire risk across the ZIP that didn’t vote for the campus.
Underwriters price the megawatts — councils should price the neighbors.
“Tax base for schools” without a household check is a bond story, not a kid story.
If the campus drinks the aquifer, the ZIP gets a water check — not just a power story.
If the campus paves the field, the farm ZIP gets a soil check — not just a ribbon photo.
Don’t approve a cooling load without publishing the household water bill path.
Two meters, one mailbox — gallons and megawatts both owe the ZIP.
